Jointly estimate a group-level choice-model shape and refine the group embedding

estimate_group_alpha.Rd

run_group_embedding_from_list always fits the group embedding under the crowd-kernel choice model (\(\alpha = 1\) on the Student-t continuum used throughout this package's recovery/validation work: \(\alpha = 1\) is exactly crowd-kernel \(\mu = 1\), \(\alpha \to \infty\) is the exact Gaussian limit). This function takes that fit as a starting point and alternates, via coordinate ascent, between (1) re-estimating \(\alpha\) by profiled maximum likelihood with the embedding held fixed, and (2) refitting the embedding under the current \(\alpha\), warm-started from the previous iteration – the group-level analogue of the per-participant joint estimation done by condor_joint_manifold_workflow.py's update step (vignette("condor_workflows_vignette"), Workflow 4), but simpler: there is only one \(\alpha\) and one embedding to estimate, so no cross-participant pooling or empirical-Bayes shrinkage is needed.

Usage

estimate_group_alpha(
  triplet_list,
  warm_start,
  max_epochs = 50000L,
  tolerance = 1e-04,
  tol_window = 10000L,
  seed = 222L,
  device = NULL,
  norm_penalty = 0,
  alpha_test_frac = 0.5,
  max_outer = 15L,
  tol_log_alpha = 0.05,
  alpha_grid = 10^seq(log10(2e-04), log10(2e+06), length.out = 140),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

triplet_list

A named list of data frames, one per participant, as returned by get.combined – the same object passed to run_group_embedding_from_list to produce warm_start. Must contain a usable sampleSet column (see Details); no longer requires sampleAlg == "validation" trials (see the section above).

warm_start

Numeric matrix giving the starting embedding: one row per item (row names = item names) and d columns, typically the embedding returned by a prior call to run_group_embedding_from_list on the same triplet_list. Required – this function refines an already-fit embedding rather than fitting one from scratch. d is taken from ncol(warm_start).

max_epochs, tolerance, tol_window, device, norm_penalty

Same meaning as the matching arguments of run_group_embedding_from_list, applied to every embedding-refit step.

seed

Integer random seed, used for the train/test shuffling fallback (when triplet_list has no usable sampleSet split), for the alpha_test_frac split of the test pool (see above), and as the embedding fit's random_state at every outer iteration.

alpha_test_frac

Proportion of the sampleSet == "test" pool set aside to profile \(\alpha\), drawn once (not re-split per outer iteration) via sample_internal_test. The remaining 1 - alpha_test_frac continues to do early stopping for the embedding refit. Must satisfy 0 < alpha_test_frac < 1. Default 0.5.

max_outer

Maximum number of coordinate-ascent iterations. Default 15.

tol_log_alpha

Convergence threshold on the log scale: stop once the re-estimated \(\alpha\) changes by less than this between iterations. Default 0.05.

alpha_grid

Candidate \(\alpha\) values for the profiled maximum-likelihood step at each iteration.

verbose

Logical; print the alpha-test/checkpoint-selection split sizes once up front, then one line of progress per outer iteration. Default TRUE.

Value

A named list with seven elements:

embedding

Numeric matrix, the final refit embedding (item names as row names, dim_0/dim_1/... columns).

alpha

Final estimated \(\alpha\).

log_alpha

log(alpha).

ci

95\ \(\alpha\) at the final iteration.

history

Data frame with one row per outer iteration: iter, alpha, ll_alpha_test (log-likelihood on the alpha-test pool at the re-estimated \(\alpha\)), acc_alpha_test (accuracy on that same pool), epoch (embedding-refit stopping epoch), and delta_log_alpha.

n_test_fit

Row count of the sub-pool used for the embedding refit's own early stopping.

n_alpha_test

Row count of the sub-pool used to profile \(\alpha\).

Details

Iteration stops once the re-estimated \(\alpha\) changes by less than tol_log_alpha (on the log scale) from the previous iteration, or after max_outer iterations, whichever comes first.

Where alpha is profiled from, and why not sampleAlg == "validation"

\(\alpha\) must be re-estimated at each iteration on trials that never influenced the embedding – profiling it on the same trials the embedding was just shaped to fit (directly, via the gradient step, or indirectly, via early-stopping checkpoint selection) would let the \(\alpha\) estimate chase sample-specific noise rather than measuring real choice-model shape. An earlier version of this function used sampleAlg == "validation" trials for this, since those are this package's existing convention for a trial pool nothing else ever touches. That has a real cost on datasets where validation trials are the whole point of calling this function in the first place: it leaves nothing genuinely untouched afterward to report the finished (embedding, \(\alpha\)) pair's quality against, since the one trial pool designed for that (get.hoacc's trialtype = "validation") has itself just been used as a tuning input.

The actual requirement for a clean \(\alpha\)-profiling pool is disjointness from whatever selected the embedding – it does not have to be literally labeled sampleAlg == "validation". This function instead splits the sampleSet == "test" pool itself (via sample_internal_test, the same mechanism estimate_dimensionality uses to carve internal_test out of sampleSet == "train") into two disjoint parts, fixed once for the whole coordinate-ascent run: alpha_test_frac of it is set aside purely to profile \(\alpha\) (step 1), and the rest continues to do early stopping/checkpoint selection for the embedding refit (step 2), exactly the role the full test pool would otherwise play. Neither sub-pool ever touches train. Any real sampleAlg == "validation" trials in triplet_list are therefore left completely untouched by this function – free to serve afterward as an honest, never-used final-quality check on the finished model.

The cost is the mirror image of the problem this solves: splitting test further means less data for checkpoint selection, which gets somewhat noisier. On a dataset with abundant randomly-sampled trials (the usual case for the legacy data this is meant to help with) that's a far better place to absorb the cost than shrinking an already-scarce validation pool.

What this does and does not estimate

Unlike the per-participant joint workflow, there is no population of noisy per-person \(\alpha\) estimates to shrink toward each other here – a single \(\alpha\) is estimated from the whole pooled dataset directly, with no regularization pulling it back if it is poorly identified. Check ci (the final iteration's 95\ confidence interval) before trusting the point estimate, especially on a small dataset or at large \(\alpha\) (the Student-t kernel converges to Gaussian as \(\alpha\) grows, so the profile likelihood flattens and \(\alpha\) becomes harder to pin down precisely, even though alpha-test accuracy itself is structurally insensitive to \(\alpha\) for this choice-model family and so cannot reveal this on its own).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
grp <- run_group_embedding_from_list(icon_triplets, d = 3L)
joint <- estimate_group_alpha(icon_triplets, warm_start = grp$embedding)
joint$alpha
joint$history

# Any real sampleAlg == "validation" trials in icon_triplets are left
# untouched by the call above -- safe to use afterward for an honest
# final check, e.g.:
# get.hoacc(joint$embedding, icon_triplets[[1]], trialtype = "validation")
} # }
